name: S-Class Bravo
body:
What Are S-Class Characters?

S-class characters began as a request from Kenneth Zike. They are built using the summoner class, as originally presented, as the basis against which all other classes are balanced. The “S” in this case stands for both summoner and, as a more appropriate in-world reference, superior.

If you have played—or GM’d for—a summoner and felt it was fine as is, you should have no problem running with an s-class character.

Special Thanks to Ciaran Barnes, Steven D. Russell, and Rite Publishing for creating the original bravo, and for allowing us to add it to our s-class character options.

S-class bravos are cunning, charismatic heroes of varied pasts depending on the regions from which they hail. They might be a sword-dancing captain of a ship, a wuxia warrior, or a gentleman adventurer seeking the heights of wealth, power, and infamy.

Role: S-class bravos rely on their wits and wiles to get them of trouble. Failing that, they always have a preferred weapon handy and a fighting technique for almost any situation.

Note: The s-class bravo is an alternate, superior version of the bravo class. They retain all of the standard bravo progressions and options, and as such should qualify to select bravo archetypes without specific adjustments.

Alignment: Any.

Hit Die: d10.

Starting Wealth: 5d6 × 10 gp (average 175 gp.) In addition, every character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The s-class bravo’s class skills are Acrobatics (Dex), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Disguise (Cha), Escape Artist (Dex), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (local) (Int), Knowledge (nobility) (Int), Perform (Cha), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Ranks p1er Level: 4 + Int modifier.

Table: S-Class Bravo

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the s-class bravo.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

S-class bravos are proficient with all simple and martial weapons. They are proficient with light armor and shields (but not tower shields).

Feint (Ex)

An s-class bravo gains Improved Feint as a bonus feat, even if she does not meet the prerequisites. When wielding a bravo weapon, she adds her bravo level on all Bluff checks she makes to feint, as well as to the DC when another creature attempts to feint her. If she uses a shield or wields a non-bravo weapon in either hand, she adds only half her bravo level (minimum +1).

Fighting Techniques (Ex)

S-class bravos learn specialized fighting techniques by studying the styles of those who came before independently or with others like them. They use these techniques to take advantage of opponents and the terrain. A technique is often identified by the name of the sword master who developed it and an animal or concept that symbolizes its spirit. Sample fighting techniques can be found at the end of this section.

At 1st level, and every four levels thereafter an s-class bravo learns one fighting technique of her choice. She can also research and learn additional techniques during downtime (see the Identifying & Learning Fighting Techniques sidebar on the next page).

An s-class bravo can use a fighting technique she has learned in either a passive or active form, which grants a competence bonus to different skills and abilities while in either. The fighting technique ends automatically if she is immobilized or helpless. She can use either form of only one fighting technique at a time and the old one ends if she enters a new one. At 6th level and every six levels thereafter the bonus associated with fighting techniques goes up by 1, to a maximum of +5 at 18th level.

Passive Form: As a standard action, the bravo gains a +2 competence bonus to the skills or other benefits listed in her passive form. This lasts for a number of hours equal to the bravo’s Intelligence bonus (minimum 1 hour), and she can end the effect as a free action.
Active Form: As a swift action, the bravo gains the benefits listed in both her active and passive forms. This lasts for a number of rounds equal to 4 + her Intelligence bonus (if positive), and she can end the effect as a free action. At each level after 1st, the bravo can use her active form for 2 additional rounds per day.

While in her active form, an s-class bravo also gains a +2 competence bonus to AC and attacks with bravo weapons.

If her speed is reduced by encumbrance or another effect, the bravo loses these benefits until it returns to normal.

Opportune Attack (Ex)

An s-class bravo recognizes an opportunity and knows well how to take advantage of it. She adds her level as a bonus to damage rolls with bravo weapons when her target would be denied a Dexterity bonus to AC, and when she makes an attack of opportunity.

S-Class Guile

In addition to their fighting techniques, s-class bravos have guile; an intricate way in which they personalize their abilities and begin to shape techniques of their own to pass down to future generations. Like fighting techniques, guiles can be found at the end of this section.

AC Bonus (Ex)

An s-class bravo uses distracting and suggestive movement to confuse and mislead her foes. Beginning at 2nd level, an s-class bravo adds her Charisma bonus as a dodge bonus to her AC (if positive). She also gains a +1 dodge bonus to AC at 4th level and every four bravo levels thereafter, up to a maximum of +5 at 20th level. She loses these bonuses if she wears armor, or if her base speed is reduced in any way, such as from encumbrance.

Bonus Feats

At 2nd level and every four levels thereafter, an s-class bravo gains a bonus feat in addition to those gained from normal advancement. The benefits of an s-class bravo’s bonus feats apply only when her base speed is not reduced in any way, such as from armor, encumbrance. These bonus feats must be selected from those listed as Combat Feats.

Upon reaching 6th level, and every four levels thereafter (8th, 12th, and so on), an s-class bravo can choose to learn a new bonus feat in place of a bonus feat she has already learned. In effect, the bravo loses the bonus feat in exchange for the new one. The old feat cannot be one that was used as a prerequisite for another feat, prestige class, or other ability. An s-class bravo can only change one feat at any given level and must choose whether or not to swap the feat at the time she gains a new bonus feat for the level.

Engaging Feint (Ex)

At 3rd level, an s-class bravo’s prowess demands her enemy’s attention. opponents under the effect of an s-class bravo’s feint cannot make attacks of opportunity against her, and they provoke attacks of opportunity from the bravo if they make an attack that does not include her. Using an ability that targets multiple opponents does not provoke an attack of opportunity in this way, as long at the bravo is one of the targets.

Identifying & Learning Fighting Techniques

Creatures with a base attack bonus of +1 or higher easily recognize (no skill check required) one fighting technique, plus one at base attack bonus +5, +9, +13, and +17. Identifying techniques requires at least 3 full rounds of direct interaction and a successful Knowledge (history) check (DC 10 + 1/2 the bravo’s level + her Charisma modifier). A creature can also learn a bravo’s technique by researching that master for at least 1 month, spending 2,000 gp and succeeding at the above check to recognize additional fighting techniques.

Élan (Ex)

At 4th level, an s-class bravo gains a pool of points representing her skill, style, and spirit to accomplish the amazing. The number of élan in this pool is equal to 1/2 the bravo’s level + her Charisma bonus. The élan pool is replenished each morning after 8 hours of rest; these hours do not need to be consecutive.

By spending 1 point from her élan pool, an s-class bravo can use one of the following benefits:

Feint: As a swift action, she can attempt a feint.
Lunge: When using a standard action to make an attack, she can first charge up to 1/4 of her speed (minimum 5 ft.) directly towards her target. This movement does not provoke an attack of opportunity from the target.
Luck: As an immediate action, she can gain a luck bonus to a single ability check or skill check equal to half her bravo level, as long as the check represents a span of time of no greater than 1 minute. 3
Parry: when an opponent makes a melee attack against the bravo, she can expend a use of an attack of opportunity to attempt to parry that attack. She makes an attack roll as if she were making an attack of opportunity; for each size category the attacking creature is larger than the bravo, the bravo takes a –2 penalty on this roll. If her result is greater than the attacking creature’s result, the creature’s attack automatically misses. The bravo must declare the use of this ability after the creature’s attack is announced, but before its attack roll is made.
Riposte: As an immediate action, after a successful parry, she can make an attack against the creature whose attack she parried, provided that creature is within her reach.

Amazing Élan: At 8th level, By spending 2 points from her élan pool, an s-class bravo can use one of the following benefits:

Opportunity: As a swift action, she does not provoke attacks of opportunity for one round.
Rapid Action: As an immediate action, she can use a move action. This counts as holding her action.
Surprise Maneuver: She can attempt a combat maneuver against the same target before or after making an attack of opportunity (her choice).
Compound Attack (Ex)

At 6th level, by strategically performing a series of false attacks against her enemy, an s-class bravo gains an advantage. As a standard action, she can either make a single attack with a bravo weapon, rolling twice and using the highest result; or she can attempt to feint two opponents.

Improved Compound Attack: At 11th level, she can roll three times or attempt to feint three opponents.

Greater Compound Attack: At 16th level, she can roll four times or attempt to feint four opponents.

Debilitating Attack (Ex)

At 7th level, once per round, when an s-class bravo makes a successful attack with a bravo weapon, she can force her opponent to make a Fortitude save (DC = 10 + 1/2 the bravo’s level + her Intelligence modifier). An opponent that succeeds at its save is immune to that bravo’s debilitating attack for 24 hours. If the creature fails its saving throw, the bravo can spend 1 point from her élan point to inflict 2 points of ability damage to one ability score of her choice. If she’s using a fighting technique, the bravo can choose to use that technique’s debilitating effect instead.

An effect caused by debilitating attack can be removed with a successful Heal skill check (as a standard action with the same DC), or one of the following spells: cleanse, heal, greater restoration, limited wish, miracle, regenerate, restoration, or wish. The accept affliction spell will transfer it to the caster, while surmount affliction will suspend the effect for the duration of the spell. The regeneration monster ability also negates this effect, although fast healing does not. Ability damage can also heal as normal.

Deadly Feint (Ex)

At 12th level, an s-class bravo is a deadly force in any battle fought on her own terms. At the start of each of her turns, as a free action, the bravo chooses between the ribs or heavy-handed and gains the chosen benefit against creatures under the effect of her feint until she chooses the other.

Between the Ribs: Bravo weapons the bravo wields increase their natural critical threat range by 1 (to a maximum range of 18-20) before applying the benefits of effects such as the Improved Critical feat or the keen magic weapon property.

Heavy-Handed: Bravo weapons the bravo wields increase their natural critical multiplier by 1 (to a maximum multiplier of x4) before applying the benefits of feats or other effects that would increase her weapon’s critical multiplier.

Immediate Adaptation (Ex)

The greatest s-class bravos adapt to danger before it strikes. Beginning at 15th level, an s-class bravo can enter a fighting technique as an immediate action before rolling initiative.

Master of Five Styles (Ex)

Having mastered the techniques of the greatest swordmasters, she is a master in her own right and blends them together seamlessly. Beginning at 19th level, an s-class bravo can enter the active form of a fighting technique without ending the effects of another, thereby gaining the benefits of each. The effects do not stack. Using more than one fighting technique in this way consumes a proportionate number of additional rounds or uses. When she is using more than one fighting technique and uses debilitating attack, she chooses which fighting technique determines the effect.

True Élan (Ex)

At 20th level, an s-class bravo’s élan is nigh unstoppable.

She gains 1 point of élan at the start of each of her turns that lasts until the end of her turn.

Favored Class Bonuses

Instead of receiving an additional skill rank or hit point whenever they gain a level in a favored class, some ancestries have the option of choosing from a number of other bonuses, depending upon their favored classes. The following options are available to the listed ancestry who have bravo as their favored class, and unless otherwise stated, the bonus applies each time you select the listed favored class reward.

Drakorin: 1/4 times per day, the bravo can spend 1 élan to recharge and use your breath weapon as a standard action.
Dwarf: Add +1/6 to the competence bonuses granted by the bravo’s fighting technique.
Elf: Add +1 to the bravo’s base speed. In combat this option has no effect unless the bravo has selected it five times (or another increment of five). This bonus stacks with the monk’s fast movement class feature and applies under the same conditions as that feature.
Gnome: Add 1/3 point to the bravo’s élan pool.
God-Blooded: The bravo can use her active form for +1 additional round per day.
Halfling: The bravo’s passive form lasts for +1 hour, to a maximum of 24 hours.
Human: Choose one—Gain 1/3 of an additional fighting technique; or add 1/3 point to the bravo’s élan pool.
Orc: Add +1/3 on critical hit confirmation rolls made with bravo weapons (maximum bonus of +5). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Sample Fighting Techniques

The fighting techniques presented here are available to all bravos, not just s-class bravos. For more techniques, please refer to the standard bravo source material.

Draco (Dragon)

Prerequisite(s): Appraise 1 rank, Knowledge (arcana) 1 rank.

When the bravo selects this fighting technique, add Appraise and Knowledge (arcana) to her list of class skills.

Passive Form: Appraise, Knowledge (arcana)
Active Form: All Strength-based checks
Debilitating Effect: The target takes a –2 penalty on attack rolls. In addition, the target takes an additional –2 penalty on all attack rolls it makes against the bravo. At 10th level and 16th level, the penalty on attack rolls made against the bravo increases by –2 (to a total maximum of –8).
Kesel (Shark)
Passive Form: Intimidate, Swim
Active Form: Increase the bravo’s swim speed by 5-feet per +1 bonus. She can attack under water using her bravo weapon with no penalties.
Debilitating Effect: The target suffers bleed damage equal to the bravo’s level at the beginning of each turn. This bleeding can be stopped by a successful Heal skill check (DC = 10 + 1/2 the bravo’s level + her Intelligence modifier) or through the application of any magical healing.
Paetier (Griffin)

Prerequisite(s): Handle Animal 1 rank, Knowledge (nature) 1 rank.

When the bravo selects this fighting technique, add Handle Animal and Knowledge (nature) to her list of class skills.

Passive Form: Handle Animal, Knowledge (nature)
Active Form: All Wisdom-based checks
Debilitating Effect: The target becomes bewildered, taking a –2 penalty to AC. The target takes an additional –2 penalty to AC against all attacks made by the bravo. At 10th level and 16th level, the penalty to AC against attacks made by the bravo increases by –2 (to a total maximum of –8).
Strikes (Scorpion)

Prerequisite(s): Intimidate 1 rank, Stealth 1 rank.

When the bravo selects this fighting technique, add Stealth to her list of class skills.

Passive Form: Intimidate, stealth
Active Form: When she uses the full-attack action, the bravo can make an additional attack with her bravo weapon at her highest base attack bonus, but all attacks she makes this round are at a –2 penalty. Beginning at 6th level, she can make a second additional attack with her bravo weapon as part of her full-attack action with a –5 penalty. At 11th level, she can make a third additional attack with her bravo weapon as part of her full-attack action with a –10 penalty.

This otherwise functions as the Two-Weapon Fighting, Improved Two-Weapon Fighting, and Greater Two-Weapon Fighting feats, respectively.

Debilitating Effect: All of the target’s speeds are reduced by half (to a minimum of 5 feet). In addition, the target cannot take a 5-foot step.

Sytsevich (Rhino)
Passive Form: Initiative checks and CMD against larger opponents
Active Form: Combat maneuver bonus
Debilitating Effect: sickened
Guiles

Standard bravos can select a guile in place of their bonus feats, AC bonus, greater compound attack, and true élan.

Court Jester

The court jester plays the fool so others can take the spotlight. She gets her work done behind the scenes while nobody pays her any attention.

Superior Feinting (Ex)

At 1st level, the bravo always adds her full bravo level when feinting, even if she uses a shield or wields a nonbravo weapon. By spending at least 1 minute to make herself look and act out of place or absurd, the bravo can feint any target, even non-humans, animals, and mindless creatures, without penalty. Because the change is more than just visual, it always requires 1 minute regardless of how the bravo accomplishes the change, and it lasts until the bravo rests or changes her appearance back to normal.

Quick Change: At 7th level, the bravo can change her appearance as a full-round action.

Immediate Change: At 17th level, by changing her mannerisms and how she holds herself, the bravo can gain the effects of changing her appearance as an immediate action when she attempts to feint a creature.

Sneak Attack (Ex)

Any time the bravo would add her opportune attack damage, she can choose instead to add 1d6 sneak attack damage. This otherwise functions as the rogue’s sneak attack ability. The bravo increases her sneak attack damage by 1d6 at 4th, 7th, 10th, 13th, 16th, and 19th level, to a maximum of 7d6 sneak attack damage at 19th level.

Evasion (Ex)

At 4th level, the bravo can avoid damage from many area-effect attacks. If the bravo succeeds at a Reflex saving throw against an attack that normally deals half damage on a successful save, she instead takes no damage. Evasion can be used only if the bravo is wearing light armor or no armor. A helpless bravo does not gain the benefit of evasion.

Improved Evasion: At 13th level, the bravo’s evasion ability improves. She still takes no damage on successful Reflex saving throws against attacks, but henceforth she takes only half damage on failed saves. A helpless bravo does not gain the benefit of improved evasion.

One-Upmanship (Ex)

At 10th level, the bravo can spend 1 point from her élan pool as a free action before attacking a foe with her bravo weapon. If the attack hits, the bravo can interrupt the target’s resources. If the bravo successfully damages the target of her attack, that opponent’s cost to activate abilities with élan increases by 1 point for 1 hour. If the bravo spends 2 points from her élan pool, she can use this ability to affect the target’s arcane pool, arcane reservoir, grit points, ki pool, inspiration, or panache points instead of its élan pool. The effects of this ability do not stack, but multiple hits increase the duration by 1 hour for each hit.

Gentleman Adventurer

The gentleman adventurer prefers discourse to direct conflict whenever possible. Her incredible luck with bravo weapons is easily mistaken as skill unless one watches closely.

Gentleman’s Combat Training

At 1st level, the bravo gains Catch Off-Guard and Throw Anything as bonus feats. She treats improvised weapons as bravo weapons.

Improvised Weapon Mastery

At 7th level, the bravo gains Improvised Weapon Mastery as a bonus feat.

Proper Discourse (Ex)

The bravo can use Diplomacy to feint, and gains a competence bonus to initiative checks equal to her Charisma modifier.

As Luck Would Have It (Ex)

At 4th level, the bravo has a knack for picking the most convenient weapon when she must fight. When the bravo uses an improvised weapon as her bravo weapon, it counts as a magic weapon for the purpose of overcoming a creature’s Damage Reduction.

At 7th level, she also treats her improvised weapon as being both cold iron and silver. At 10th level, she can affect creatures with alignment-based DR. At 17th level, she treats improvised weapons as adamantine, and at 20th level, she can overcome any Damage Reduction, even DR /–.

Thought-Provoking Conversation (Ex)

At 4th level, the bravo can spend 1 point from her élan pool as a swift action to present a paradox to a creature within 30 feet or a philosophical question to herself to give her a fresh perspective.

Paradox: The creature must succeed at a Will save (DC = 10 + 1/2 the bravo’s level + her Charisma modifier) or be confused for 1 round. This is a mind-affecting, language-dependent effect.

Philosophical Question: The bravo must attempt a Will save (DC 15 + 1/2 her bravo level). If successful, she gains an insight bonus equal to her Charisma modifier to AC and on attack rolls, saving throws, skill checks and until the end of the round. If she fails, the bravo is instead confused for 1 round. This is a mind-affecting, language-dependent effect.

A character who can’t become confused can’t benefit from this ability.

Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

At 7th level, an s-class barbarian gains the ability to react to danger before her senses would normally allow her to do so. She cannot be caught flat-footed, nor does she lose her Dexterity bonus to AC if immobilized. An s-class barbarian with this ability can still lose her Dexterity bonus to AC if an opponent successfully uses the feint action against her.

If an s-class barbarian already has uncanny dodge from a different class, she automatically gains improved uncanny dodge (see below) instead.

Improved Uncanny Dodge: At 10th level, an s-class barbarian can no longer be flanked. This defense denies enemies the ability to sneak attack the barbarian by flanking her, unless the attacker has at least 4 more levels in a class that provides sneak attack than the barbarian has barbarian levels.

Philosophy of Battle (Ex)

At 13th level, the bravo can spend an additional point from her élan pool when using thought-provoking conversation.

If she does, she can present a paradox to a number of creatures of her choice within 30 feet equal to her Charisma modifier; or she can pose a philosophical question to one of her allies within 30 feet.

Wandering Hero

The wandering hero seeks to root out trouble wherever she can, often stopping to help others to the detriment of her own time unless some greater, more pressing goal prevents her from doing so.

A Tough Life

The life of a wandering hero is inherently more complicated than most. At 1st level, the bravo gains Endurance and Toughness as bonus feats.

Traveler’s Fare (Ex)

At 1st level, rumors of the bravo’s travels have already reached far and wide, in part because of her own ability to share them. The bravo can always share a good story for a hot meal or a place to sleep. She can use Bluff or Diplomacy in place of Profession to earn a living, and can make one such check automatically upon entering a settlement for the first time. Once she has done this in a specific location, the bravo can’t do so again until she spends at least one month away, making new stories to share.

Word of Mouth: At 7th level, the bravo’s exploits have begun to reach others even without her help. Creatures that recognize the bravo are automatically friendly or unfriendly to her if they would normally start as indifferent, and the bravo automatically adds her passive form bonus to checks to influence those creatures’ attitudes with Diplomacy. In friendly territory, the quality of living the bravo can earn is increased so that she can cover expenses for herself and up to four others where normally she could only vouch for herself. At 17th level, creatures that would start as friendly with the bravo start as helpful instead.

Traveling Light (Ex)

At 4th level, the bravo’s experience on the roads and open seas of the world greatly improve her metabolism.

As long as she has at least 1 point remaining in her élan pool, the bravo needs to eat and drink only 1/4 as often as normal, needs only 2 hours of sleep each night (including to replenish her élan pool), and can hold her breath for up to 1 hour per point of Constitution. As a move action, she can spend 1 point from her élan pool to enter a state of suspended animation, falling unconscious and appearing dead to all senses. At the time she enters this state, she indicates a preset period of time or a triggering condition, after which she awakens.

We Can Do This, Together (Ex)

At 7th level, as an immediate action before she rolls a saving throw against a targeted effect that also targets other allies or an area effect whose area includes other allies, the bravo can spend any number of points from her élan pool and designate a number of adjacent allies equal to the number of points spent. The bravo rolls one saving throw for each designated ally, using her bonus instead of the ally’s.

For each successful saving throw, the corresponding ally treats the effect as if that ally had succeeded at the saving throw, and for each saving throw failed, the corresponding ally treats the effect as if that ally had failed the saving throw.

If the bravo fails any of the saving throws (including her own original saving throw), the bravo treats the effect as if she had failed the saving throw.

Insightful Words (Ex)

At 10th level, the bravo can spend 2 points from her élan pool as an immediate action to give another ally within 30 feet just the right word of advice to prevent disaster. If the ally can hear the bravo, she can reroll a single attack roll or saving throw. The ally must take the second result, even if it is worse.

Call to Heroism (Ex)

At 10th level, the bravo can draw out the inner hero herself or a single willing ally within 30 feet, granting extra fighting capability. For every three levels the bravo attains beyond 10th, she can target one additional ally (up to a maximum of four at 19th level). All of the targets must be able to see and hear the bravo’s call to heroism.

A creature called to heroism gains 2 bonus Hit Dice (d10s), the commensurate number of temporary hit points (apply the target’s Constitution modifier, if any, to these bonus Hit Dice), a +2 competence bonus on attack rolls, and a +1 competence bonus on Fortitude saves. The bonus Hit Dice count as regular Hit Dice for determining the effect of spells that are Hit Dice dependent.

Inspire greatness is a mind-affecting ability and it relies on audible and visual components.

Tongue of the Sun and Moon (Ex)

At 13th level, the bravo can understand and speak with any living creature, as if under a permanent tongues effect.

Wave Dancer

The wave dancer is always light on her feet, focusing her guile on greater mobility and agility when in battle. Of any bravo, she is the most likely to be found on a ship sailing the open seas.

Wave Dancer Combat Training

At 1st level, the bravo gains Mobility and Sea Legs as bonus feats, even if she doesn’t meet the prerequisites. At 4th level, she also gains Spring Attack.

Dancer’s Cunning (Ex)

The bravo can treat her Charisma score as her Intelligence score for the purpose of meeting the prerequisites of combat feats. In addition, she can attempt a Perform (dance) check instead of a Bluff check to feint in combat, and her bravo weapons are considered to have the performance weapon special quality.

Fluttering Steps (Ex)

At 4th level, the bravo can spend 1 point from her élan pool as a swift action to quickly traverse short distances.

This increases the bravo’s base land speed by 30 feet for 1 minute.

Wave Dance (Ex)

At 4th level, the bravo can perform a wave dance as a full-attack action. When she does, she is treated as having the Two-Weapon Fighting feat as long as she’s attacking with her bravo weapon and can make all relevant attacks with that weapon, but she must move at least 5 feet before or after every attack she makes. If she can’t move for any reason, the wave dance ends. At 7th level, the bravo gains use of the Improved Two-Weapon Fighting feat when using wave dance. At 13th level, she gains use of the Greater Two-Weapon Fighting feat when using wave dance.

Instead of making attacks during her wave dance, the bravo can also use combat maneuvers against the opponents she moves within range of, and she doesn’t provoke attacks of opportunity from the target of her combat maneuver.

Dance Partner

Starting at 10th level, when the bravo uses wave dance and moves into a flanking position against an opponent during that action, the opponent remains flanked by the bravo until the start of the bravo’s next turn, even if she leaves that space as part of her wave dance. If the opponent moves more than 5 feet away from its current position, or the creature with which the bravo flanks the opponent moves more than 5 feet from it, the flanking condition ends.

The bravo can flank up to two creatures in this way at a time at 10th level, three creatures at 17th level, and four creatures at 20th level.

High Jump (Ex)

At 7th level, the bravo adds her level as a bonus on all Acrobatics checks to jump, both for vertical jumps and horizontal jumps. In addition, she always counts as having a running start when attempting Acrobatics checks to jump.

By spending 1 point from her élan pool as a swift action, the bravo gains a +20 bonus on Acrobatics checks to jump for 1 round.

Light Steps (Ex)

At 7th level, the bravo can move effortlessly across nearly any surface. Whenever she activates her fluttering steps, she can also ignore all difficult terrain. In addition, while active, she can cross any solid surface, even if it would normally not support her weight. This does not allow her to walk on liquids.

Action Before Thought (Ex)

At 10th level, the bravo can spend 2 points from her élan pool as a free action as part of rolling initiative to roll twice on the initiative check and take the higher result.

Water Sprint (Ex)

At 10th level, the bravo can spend 1 point from her élan pool as a swift action to gain the ability to walk on water, as if under the effects of water walk. Once activated, this ability lasts for 1 minute per bravo level.

Slow Fall (Su)

At 13th level, when she is within arm’s reach of a wall, the bravo can use it to slow her descent by expending 1 point from her élan pool. When she uses this ability, she takes no damage from the fall (as if using feather fall), but she must be adjacent to a wall for the length of the fall (although this can be used to reduce the damage from a fall if only part of it is adjacent to a wall).

Wuxia Master

The wuxia master uses monk weapons in combat and a keen attention to detail when accomplishing tasks. She is a difficult opponent to pin down because of her defensive talents and spiritual training.

Wuxia Combat Training

A wuxia master gains Improved Unarmed Strike as a bonus feat, and is proficient with all monk weapons. She treats her unarmed strikes and monk weapons as bravo weapons.

Still Mind (Ex)

At 4th level, the bravo gains a +2 bonus on saving throws against enchantment spells and effects.

High Jump (Ex)

At 7th level, the bravo adds her level as a bonus on all Acrobatics checks to jump, both for vertical jumps and horizontal jumps. In addition, she always counts as having a running start when attempting Acrobatics checks to jump.

By spending 1 point from her élan pool as a swift action, the bravo gains a +20 bonus on Acrobatics checks to jump for 1 round.

Purity of Body (Ex)

At 5th level, the bravo gains immunity to all diseases, including supernatural and magical diseases.

Wind Jump (Ex)

At 9th level, the bravo can spend 1 point from her élan pool as a move action to grant herself a fly speed (with perfect maneuverability) equal to her base land speed. She must end her movement each round on solid ground (or some other surface that can support her weight) or fall as normal. Once activated, this ability lasts for 1 minute.

One Touch (Ex)

At 13th level, as long as she has at least 1 point remaining in her élan pool, as a standard action, the bravo can use a bravo weapon to make an attack against a foe as a touch attack. She adds 1/2 her bravo level as a bonus on the damage roll. She can spend 1 point from her élan pool to double this bonus for that attack.

Diamond Soul (Ex)

At 13th level, the bravo can spend 2 points from her élan pool as a swift action to gain Spell Resistance equal to her bravo level + 10. This Spell Resistance lasts for a number of rounds equal to the bravo’s level.

Timeless Body (Ex)

At 17th level, the bravo no longer takes penalties to her ability scores for aging and cannot be magically aged. Any such penalties that she has already taken, however, remain in place. Age bonuses still accrue, and the bravo still dies of old age when her time is up.

Flawless Mind

At 19th level, the bravo gains total control over her mental faculties. Whenever she attempts a Will save, she can roll twice and take the better result. If she fails a Will saving throw against a spell or effect that has a duration longer than 1 hour, the bravo can attempt a new saving throw at the end of each hour to end the effect.

Perfect Self

At 20th level, the bravo becomes a magical creature.

She is forevermore treated as an outsider rather than a humanoid (or whatever her original creature type was) for the purpose of spells and magical effects.
She gains Damage Reduction 10/chaotic.
Unlike other outsiders, the bravo can still be brought back from the dead as if she were a member of her previous creature type.
She gains the ability to enter a state of perfect calm.

During this time, the bravo can take no actions, but she does regain élan at the rate of 1 point per 10 minutes spent at calm. She cannot use this ability to gain an amount of élan in excess of her maximum.
